title: Sky's debt-ceiling circuit breakers stop new risk without trapping existing users
content:
Both GroupedLineWipeSpell (A.1.10.5.2.2.2.1) and MultiLineWipeSpell (A.1.10.5.2.2.3.1) describe the same effect in the same terms: debt ceilings are set to zero, and "Users will still be able to exit their positions, but no new debt will be allowed to be created."

The asymmetry is the design. A line wipe blocks the inflow of new exposure while leaving the outflow open — it stops the problem growing without converting a risk event into a liquidity trap. The scenarios given are a stablecoin depeg or a hack of the protocol backing the collateral, i.e. cases where the collateral's value is suddenly untrustworthy and additional borrowing against it would socialize the loss.

This contrasts with the liquidation-stopping spells (GroupedClipBreakerSpell, MultiClipBreakerSpell), which halt an active process, and with the OSM freezes (A.1.10.5.2.2.1.1, A.1.10.5.2.2.3.3), which stop bad prices from being registered so "the problem [can] be fixed with no impact on the system."

The generalizable principle: an emergency measure that also blocks exit converts a solvency question into a panic. Preserving the exit path is what lets a circuit breaker be pulled early and on suspicion rather than only on confirmed loss.
description: Line-wipe Standby Spells set debt ceilings to zero, so no new debt can be created while users can still exit their positions; the freeze is one-directional by design.
